import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 258

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/258](https://www.erdosproblems.com/258)
- [Ch26] P. Chojecki and GPT-5.4 Pro, [Erdős problem 258](https://www.ulam.ai/research/erdos258.pdf) (2026)
- [St26] ster-oc, [Lean formalisation of Erdős problem 258](https://live.lean-lang.org/#project=mathlib-v4.28.0&url=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ster-oc/2b7adcf9d753cf6e29d782f7374cc57e/raw/689a8483895cbe147634dfbf2d7b1db93a3b5b5f/Erdos258.lean) (2026)
-/

namespace Erdos258

/--
Let $a_n \to \infty$ be a sequence of non-zero natural numbers. Is
$\sum_n \frac{d(n)}{(a_1 ... a_n)}$ irrational, where $d(n)$ is the number of divisors of $n$?

This was proved affirmatively by Chojecki and GPT-5.4 Pro [Ch26], and formalised in Lean
by ster-oc [St26].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://live.lean-lang.org/#project=mathlib-v4.28.0&url=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ster-oc/2b7adcf9d753cf6e29d782f7374cc57e/raw/689a8483895cbe147634dfbf2d7b1db93a3b5b5f/Erdos258.lean"]
theorem erdos_258 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, 2 ≤ a n) →
    Filter.Tendsto a Filter.atTop Filter.atTop →
    Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), ((n + 1).divisors.card / ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (n + 1), a i)) := by
  sorry


/--
Let $2 \leq a_1 \leq a_2 \leq \cdots$ be a monotone sequence with $a_n \to \infty$.
Is $\sum_n \frac{d(n)}{a_1 \cdots a_n}$ irrational, where $d(n)$ is the number of divisors of $n$?

Solution: True (proved by Erdős and Straus [ErSt71], Lemma 2.2 and Theorem 2.13).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_258.variants.monotone : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, 2 ≤ a n) → Monotone a →
    Filter.Tendsto a Filter.atTop Filter.atTop →
    Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), ((n + 1).divisors.card / ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (n + 1), a i)) := by
  sorry


/--
Is $\sum_n \frac{d(n)}{t^n}$ irrational, where $t ≥ 2$ is an integer.

Solution: True (proved by Erdős, see Erdős Problems website)
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_258.variants.constant : answer(True) ↔ ∀ t ≥ (2 : ℕ),
    Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), ((n + 1).divisors.card / t^(n + 1))) := by
  sorry

end Erdos258

findings.description: The solution citation in the docstring names “Lemma 2.2 and Theorem 2.13” of Erdős–Straus. There is no Theorem 2.13 there: (2.13) is an equation within the proof of Lemma 2.2. The monotone irrationality result is Theorem 2.23. The Lean statement itself is correct.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős and Straus, Some number theoretic results, Pacific J. Math. 36 (1971), https://msp.org/pjm/1971/36-3/pjm-v36-n3-p07-s.pdf: equation (2.13) appears on p. 640; Theorem 2.23 on p. 641 states that series (2.1) is irrational whenever 2 ≤ a₁ ≤ a₂ ≤ ⋯.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the citation with “[ErSt71], Theorem 2.23,” or cite the constituent Lemmas 2.2 and 2.14. No change to the theorem statement is needed.

status_issues.recorded: An unconditional `formal_proof using lean4` annotation points to the ster-oc gist, and the docstring reports the Lean formalization without qualification.
status_issues.source_status: The cited Lean proof establishes the result only modulo the unformalized Tao–Teräväinen theorem. The affirmative mathematical solution and `research solved` category remain correct; it is the unconditional formal-proof record that overstates the linked proof.
status_issues.evidence: The exact cited source, https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ster-oc/2b7adcf9d753cf6e29d782f7374cc57e/raw/689a8483895cbe147634dfbf2d7b1db93a3b5b5f/Erdos258.lean, explicitly says “modulo the deep Tao–Teräväinen theorem … stated here without proof” and declares `axiom tao_teravainen` at lines 311–314. Its main theorem uses that axiom through `tao_teravainen_divisors_le`. After local tactic/API compatibility edits for the available Lean version, `#print axioms erdos_258` confirmed `[propext, tao_teravainen, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`; the adapted proof's statement was also checked to imply the file's exact statement.
status_issues.suggested_change: Remove the unconditional formal_proof annotation, or explicitly record a conditional formalization with the Tao–Teräväinen input named and stated as its assumption. Qualify the docstring accordingly. Retain `category research solved` and `answer(True)`.

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement requires 2 ≤ a n at every natural-number index, whereas the cited 2026 note allows arbitrary positive integers aₙ, indexed from 1, tending to infinity.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Choose N such that aₙ ≥ 2 for n > N. Double the first N positive-indexed terms to obtain bₙ, leaving later terms unchanged. Then bₙ ≥ 2 and bₙ → ∞. For m ≥ N, the denominator products satisfy Q_b(m) = 2^N Q_a(m). Both series converge, and consequently S_a = 2^N S_b + r for a rational finite-prefix correction r. Irrationality is unchanged by this nonzero rational scaling and rational translation. The converse follows immediately by restricting to bases at least 2. The unused value at index 0 can be chosen freely without changing any summand. The complete equivalence was proved as review_source_iff_file in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, using only standard axioms.

review.notes: No substantive mathematical misformalization was found in the three theorem statements. Lean checks confirmed real division, correct positive indexing, nonzero denominators, small divisor counts and first terms, and satisfiable hypotheses. A sorry-free summability proof covers all three series, excluding misuse of tsum's divergent-series default. The direct Erdős Problems page and forum returned Cloudflare challenges despite descriptive User-Agent headers; the cited note and primary papers supplied the mathematical statements and affirmative resolution. All experiments and proof adaptations are under /workspace/review/; the reviewed file matches its committed contents.
